The Jungle is one of the most famous muckraking novels in modern history. Set in Chicago at the dawn of the 20th century, it tells the story of an immigrant Lithuanian family trying to make it in a new world both cruel and full of opportunity. Their struggles are in part a vehicle for Sinclair to shine a spotlight on the monstrous conditions of the meatpacking industry, to expose the brutal exploitation of immigrants and workers, and to espouse his more socialist worldview. The novel is in part responsible for the passage of the revolutionary Meat Inspection Act and the Pure Food and Drug act, and thus the establishment of the modern-day Food and Drug administration in the U.S. Its impact is in no small part due to the direct and powerful prose Sinclair employs: the horrors of commercial meat production are presented in full and glistening detail, and the tragedies and misfortunes of the Rudkus family are direct and relatable even today.

ia_description: Fictional works, of different literary periods, which share a common perception of man can be explicated and compared with each other to illustrate a continuing tradition in American literature. Such a basis for comparison exists between Hawthorne's romance, "The Scarlet Letter," which appeared in 1850, and Henry James' fantasy, "The Beast in the Jungle," published 53 years later. Both works attempt to portray the "essential truth of the human heart" by evoking an awareness of the common doom or destiny that all men share in their isolation from each other, an isolation aggravated by the sin of pride. Although differences in surface structure, psychological point of view, use of symbol and image, and methods of execution exist between the two works, each novelist places his characters in a situation which dramatizes the effect of erring, but free-willed, action. Sheena: Queen Of The Jungle (1984) The 1984 film Sheena: Queen Of The Jungle is a fantasy action film, inspired by the Tarzan stories. It was directed by John Guillermin and stars Tanya Roberts in the lead role. The movie was a box-office failure and won several awards for the worst film of 1984. The film was critically panned as well, but has since garnered significant success as a cult film. Two geologists exploring Africa are tragically killed, and their daughter is orphaned. She is adopted by a native tribe (called the Zambouli) and named Sheena from an ancient prophecy. Sheena (played by Tanya Roberts ) grows up in the jungle and can telepathically communicate with animals. The land of the Zambouli is rich with titanium, and a few reporters stumble on a foreign conspiracy to exploit the land. They see Sheena rescue a member of the Zambouli. Meanwhile, mercenaries are coming into the land to kill the Zamboulis. One of the reporters, Vic (played by Ted Wass) decides to join Sheena in stopping the mercenaries and their leader, Prince Otwani (played by Trevor Thomas). ia_description: Title Pjetër Pani (Peter Pan) – James Matthew Barrie (Xhems Metju Bari) – Albanian Translation by Ramiz Kelmendi – Rilindja, Prishtina, 1959 | Pjetër Pani – Përkthim Shqip – Rilindja, Prishtinë, 1959 Creator James Matthew Barrie (Xhems Metju Bari) Author James Matthew Barrie Translator / Përkthyes Ramiz Kelmendi Editor / Redaktor Fuat Ostrozubi Illustrator / Ilustrues Miomir Zubiq Publisher / Botues Rilindja Place / Vendi Prishtinë, Kosovo (Former Yugoslavia) Year / Viti 1959 Language / Gjuha Albanian (Shqip) Mediatype texts Collection opensource Description English Peter Pan is one of the world's most beloved classics of children's fantasy literature, written by Scottish author James Matthew Barrie . This rare Albanian-language edition, titled Pjetër Pani , was published in Prishtina in 1959 by Rilindja . The Albanian translation was prepared by Ramiz Kelmendi , edited by Fuat Ostrozubi , and illustrated by Miomir Zubiq . The story follows Peter Pan, the boy who never grows up, together with Wendy Darling, John, Michael, Tinker Bell, Captain Hook, the Lost Boys and the magical world of Neverland. This edition represents one of the early Albanian translations of a world literary masterpiece and is an important document of Albanian publishing history. This digital preservation copy is intended for historical research, literary studies, education, bibliography, Albanology, cultural heritage preservation, and digital library collections. Shqip Pjetër Pani është përkthimi shqip i veprës klasike botërore Peter Pan , shkruar nga autori skocez James Matthew Barrie (Xhems Metju Bari) . Ky botim i rrallë në gjuhën shqipe u botua në Prishtinë më 1959 nga Rilindja , me përkthim nga Ramiz Kelmendi , redaktim nga Fuat Ostrozubi dhe ilustrime nga Miomir Zubiq . Libri rrëfen aventurat e djaloshit që nuk rritet kurrë, Peter Pan, së bashku me Wendy Darling, John, Michael, Tinker Bell, Kapiten Hook dhe Djemtë e Humbur në botën magjike të Neverland. Ky botim përfaqëson një nga përkthimet më të hershme shqiptare të një kryevepre të letërsisë botërore dhe ka rëndësi të veçantë në historinë e botimeve shqiptare. ia_title: The Betwixt and Between: Peter Pan as a Trickster Figure
ia_subject: ["trickster", "James Matthew Barrie", "Peter Pan", "The Little White Bird", "Peter and Wendy", "Victorian England", "child"]
ia_description: The focus of the present thesis is the trickster, a mythical figure that is typically associated with Native American and African cultures. In this thesis, however, the term “trickster” is applied to Peter Pan, an iconic character of British culture, which sprang to life during the adventures of James Matthew Barrie and the Llewelyn Davies boys. The thesis challenges the assumption that the true trickster  can be found only in mythology, particularly in Native American myths. The aim is, therefore, to demonstrate that Peter Pan, although a literary figure of Western canon, can be considered a fully fledged trickster. The first part of the thesis conceptualises and clarifies the notion of this elusive figure, summarising the most important theories about this topic. The second part analyses the character of Peter Pan in terms of the typical trickster features, taking into consideration his mythological origins, the author and the narrator of the story, and the cultural context, with which every trickster is inherently connected. Specifically, the thesis explores Peter Pan’s role in subverting Victorian ideas about the child. Peter Pan’s trickster features are illustrated on the examples taken from three works, which serve as a basis for the study of Peter Pan: the novel The Little White Bird, where Peter Pan appeared for the first time; the play Peter Pan, which made this character famous; and the novel Peter and Wendy, where Peter’s nature is most apparent.

ia_description: ["xiii, 400 pages, 16 unnumbered pages of plates : 25 cm", "\"The world has long been captivated by the story of Peter Pan and the countless movies, plays, musicals, and books that retell the story of Peter, Wendy, and the Lost Boys. Now, in this revealing behind-the-scenes book, author Piers Dudgeon examines the fascinating and complex relationships among Peter Pan's creator, J.M. Barrie, and the family of boys who inspired his work. After meeting the Llewelyn Davies family in London's Kensington Garden, Barrie struck up an intense friendship with the children and their parents. The innocence of Michael, the fourth of five brothers, went on to influence the creation of Barrie's most famous character, Peter Pan. Barrie was so close to the Llewelyn Davies family that he became trustee and guardian to the boys following the deaths of their parents. Although the relationship between the boys and Barrie (and particularly between Barrie and Michael) was enduring, it was punctuated by the fiercest of tragedies. Throughout the heart-rending saga of Barrie's involvement with the Llewelyn Davies brothers, it is the figure of Michael, the most original and inspirational of their number, and yet also the one whose fate is most pitiable, that stands out. ia_description: Peter Pan est une série de bande dessinée en six volumes de Régis Loisel éditée par Vents d'Ouest de 1990 à 2004. L'histoire débute en 1887 : le jeune Peter se bat pour survivre entre une mère alcoolique et les faubourgs misérables de Londres. Son imagination et les contes du vieux Mr. Kundal sont les seuls instants de bonheur qu'il peut s'offrir au milieu de la misère et de l'absurdité du monde des adultes. Tout bascule le jour où il rencontre une petite fée égarée, Clochette, qui vient pour l'emmener dans son monde imaginaire. L'idée centrale du Peter Pan de Régis Loisel est celle que ce jeune satyre est en fait l'incarnation des croyances du passé, basée sur l'imaginaire enfantin, ce qui fait de lui la représentation même de la future personnalité de Peter Pan. 1 Londres, Vents d'Ouest, novembre 1990 2 Opikanoba, Vents d'Ouest, septembre 1992 3 Tempête, Vents d'Ouest, novembre 1994 4 Mains rouges, Vents d'Ouest, septembre 1996 5 Crochet, Vents d'Ouest, janvier 2001 6 Destins, Vents d'Ouest, octobre 2004

ia_description: Virginia Woolf's "Orlando" is an excellent example of mock biography to use in literature classes concerned with analyzing literary genres. Woolf used humor to undermine some conventions of the genre of biography and to reform biography into a shape adequate to express the life of Vita Sackville-West. An ordinary biography most likely would have to position Vita as man or woman, tragic or comic. Woolf's mock biography, however, more uncertain than it is certain, more hyperbolic than it is realistic, is the story of a man/woman's four hundred years full of gender changes, cross-dressing, lovers of both sexes, and a court case to determine her sex. It tells broad diverse tragi-comic truths about Vita that more ordinary biography might have been incapable of embracing. (RS)

ia_description: This Technical Note describes the instrument landing system (ILS) math modeling performed by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Technical Center at the request of the Southern Region. Computed data are presented showing the effects of airside terminals with simulated docked and taxiing aircraft on the performance of an ILS localizer proposed for runway 35L at the Orlando International Airport. The Southern Region is concerned that reflections from two proposed airside terminals with docked and taxiing aircraft may degrade the localizer course beyond category II/III tolerances. Modeled course structure results indicate that category II/III localizer performance should be obtained with the Wilcox Mark II, 14-element, dual-frequency log periodic antenna and both airside terminals with docked and taxiing aircraft at the currently proposed locations. Computed clearance orbit results indicate satisfactory linearity, course crossover, and signal clearance levels.

“Sister Carrie”  by Theodore Dreiser is a seminal work of American naturalism that chronicles the life of Caroline "Carrie" Meeber, a young woman who moves from her rural home to Chicago in pursuit of a better life. Initially, Carrie faces poverty and struggles to find steady employment. She becomes entangled with Charles Drouet, a charming salesman who introduces her to a more glamorous lifestyle. Eventually, she meets George Hurstwood, a middle-aged manager of a saloon, and the two embark on a romantic affair. Hurstwood steals money and persuades Carrie to flee with him to New York. However, their fortunes decline as Hurstwood's circumstances deteriorate, while Carrie begins to rise as an actress. The novel explores themes of ambition, desire, and the social forces that shape human destiny. Carrie’s journey illustrates the allure and pitfalls of the American Dream, as her material success comes at the cost of emotional fulfilment. Hurstwood, in contrast, represents the decline of those unable to adapt to changing societal pressures. Dreiser’s unflinching portrayal of economic struggles, class disparity, and moral ambiguity underscores the harsh realities of urban life at the turn of the 20th century, making  Sister Carrie  a powerful commentary on the complexities of modern existence. The North Star There are moments in every generation when the ground beneath our feet seems to shift, when the stories we have inherited about the world no longer satisfy the deeper questions of the soul. We live in such a moment now. The modern age, with its dazzling technologies and its unshakable confidence in scientific consensus, has also produced unprecedented doubt, confusion, and fragmentation. Institutions once trusted without hesitation now stand under suspicion. The very shape and structure of the world—once considered settled—has become a subject of renewed debate. In the midst of this turbulence, one ancient light remains unmoved: the North Star. While the earth is said to spin at a thousand miles per hour, orbit the sun at sixty‑six thousand, and hurtle through the galaxy at five hundred thousand, Polaris remains fixed, steady, and unchanging. Sailors trusted it. Shepherds trusted it. Civilizations aligned their temples to it. And Scripture itself speaks of a created order that is stable, purposeful, and upheld by the word of God. This book begins with a simple observation: the North Star does not move, though everything around it is said to be in constant motion. That observation is not offered as proof of any cosmological model. It is offered as a symbol—of constancy, of orientation, and of the unchanging truth found in the King James Bible, which will serve as the final authority throughout this work.
